name: Prague
title: Holidays in Prague
intro: A hilltop castle, a medieval clock that puts on a show and great-value food. Here's what Prague is like with the family, when to go and how long to stay.
facts_note: The EU is bringing in new entry checks, so check the rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: May, June and September are warm without the summer crowds. July and August are busy on the bridge and in the old town. December brings Christmas markets with roasting chestnuts and a big tree in the Old Town Square.

things.name: Prague Castle
things.blurb: The world's biggest castle complex. The grounds are free, and you can watch the changing of the guard.

things.name: Charles Bridge
things.blurb: A stone bridge lined with statues. Go early before the crowds.

things.name: Astronomical Clock
things.blurb: Figures pop out to put on a show every hour.

things.name: Petřín Hill
things.blurb: A funicular up to a mini Eiffel Tower and a mirror maze.

things.name: Prague Zoo
things.blurb: One of the best zoos in Europe, with a chairlift and gorillas.

things.name: Paddle boats
things.blurb: Hire a boat on the river from Slovanský island.

faqs.question: Is Prague good for a family holiday?
faqs.answer: Yes. The old town is compact and storybook-pretty, the trams are easy, and food is good value. Cobbles make pushchairs hard work.

faqs.question: How many nights do you need?
faqs.answer: Three or four nights covers the main sights at a family pace.

faqs.question: Do UK families need a visa?
faqs.answer: No, British passport holders can visit for up to 90 days in any 180 without a visa. New EU entry checks are being brought in, so check GOV.UK before you travel.

faqs.question: Do you need Czech money?
faqs.answer: Yes, the Czech Republic uses the koruna, not the euro. Cards work almost everywhere. Avoid the high-street exchange booths.
